topics: Structured output schema and parsing errors
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-09
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Eliot (Redwood SE), Jamal (Lead Eng - Bluehaven), Priya (PM), Hannah (CTO)

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you all taking the time. Quick agenda: SDK examples for tool calls, structured JSON output determinism, and then run through the recent test failures you sent. Anything to add, Priya?

[00:12] Priya (PM - Bluehaven): No, that covers it. We mainly want to see if the structured outputs can be made more deterministic — our ingestion pipeline chokes when the model deviates.

[00:23] Eliot (Redwood SE): Cool. I pulled up the runs you shared — thanks Jamal — and there are two obvious patterns: first, occasional trailing tokens that break JSON parse, and second, when streaming is enabled sometimes the function signature metadata arrives out of order. We'll walk through both.

[00:38] Jamal (Lead Eng): Yeah, the trailing commas and the partial close braces are the usual suspects. Our parser is strict; it won't accept anything that's not exact JSON.

[00:46] Maya: Right, so for the POC we have two levers: one is SDK-level helpers that validate and stitch streaming chunks into a final JSON; the other is model-side guidance — structured output templates and stricter function calling. Eliot, do you want to show the SDK snippet?

[00:59] Eliot: Sure. So current SDK beta supports a helper like redwood.parseStructured(response, schema) that will buffer stream chunks, attempt a best-effort repair, and also return confidence for each field. It's still early — sometimes the repair guesses wrong if the model emits natural text interleaved with JSON.

[01:18] Jamal: Can the helper do incremental parsing? We need to present partial results to our UI while the full response finishes.

[01:25] Eliot: Yes, incremental mode is supported. It yields partial objects as they become parseable. But caveat — partials can be syntactically invalid until the final chunk arrives, so we emit 'partial' flags. That worked in our internal demo but I saw your transcript logs where the client threw on the first partial.

[01:40] Priya: That's exactly the problem: our UI treats any malformed object as terminal. We might need a fallback where the SDK returns raw text and the app decides when to try parse again.

[01:50] Maya: Good call. We'll include an example where the SDK exposes both the raw stream and a repaired JSON attempt, and show the recommended app pattern. I'll add that to the artifacts. Link: https://redwood.example.com/sdk-examples/tool-calls (note: link is internal demo).

[02:05] Hannah (CTO): Quick security question — when you talk about streaming and buffering, where does that buffer live? We need to ensure nothing gets persisted improperly.

[02:12] Eliot: By default buffering is in-memory within the SDK process. For Redwood-hosted runs the transcript chunks pass through TLS and aren't stored unless you opt-in to debug logs. For Dedicated or Private deployments you control logs and we can set an option to redact or disable buffering. Also we support KMS for any persisted artifacts.

[02:30] Jamal: Ok, that's fine. On the structured output side, one of our failure cases was that the model sometimes returns arrays with mixed types — e.g., ids as numbers and strings. Any suggestions?

[02:40] Eliot: We recommend schema enforcement on the SDK side: schema field types plus an optional coercion layer. For POC I'd propose we send a small example of the schema-constraining prompt pattern we use and an SDK validator. It will coerce numbers to strings if you want, or else raise an explicit error.

[02:58] Priya: Would that affect latency? We're sensitive to per-request latency; extra validation could add a few ms maybe.

[03:04] Eliot: Validation itself is negligible — a few ms in Ruby/Go/Node. The bigger cost is if you disable streaming and rely on full response post-processing; that adds end-to-end latency equal to model response time. So prefer streaming + incremental parse.

[03:20] Maya: Which brings up batching — Jamal, you mentioned you're sending variable-length prompts; what's your typical tokens per request?

[03:28] Jamal: Right now it's around 220 tokens average, some go to 1.2k.

[03:34] Eliot: For that distribution, Redwood's default batching should be fine. If you want lower p95 latency we can dedicate a smaller bucket or pin to a dedicated node. That reduces queuing but costs more.

[03:45] Priya: Do you have an estimate for dedicated node cost for our profile?

[03:49] Maya: We'll send a ballpark. For the POC we can use burst-dedicated for predictable p95; I'll include pricing options in the follow-up.

[03:58] Hannah: Another integration question — our security team insists on SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning before any sustained access. We've got SOC2 and ISO requirements too.

[04:07] Maya: We support SSO/SAML and SCIM in the console, and for Private deployments we can integrate with your IdP directly. Our security docs (link: /security/soc2.pdf) will be included with the follow-up.

[04:18] Jamal: Back to function calling: in one failed run the model called the wrong tool — returned tool_x instead of tool_y — even though we defined clearly named functions. Is that a prompt issue or a model bug?

[04:30] Eliot: Could be both. Function selection depends on the prompt context. We recommend include explicit function signatures and call examples. Also the SDK includes an affinity setting: prefer tool by name when confidence is close. We'll send an example where you can force tool routing by tag.

[04:46] Priya: Would forcing tool routing reduce the model's ability to be flexible? We're worried about edge cases where heuristics matter.

[04:52] Eliot: It's a tradeoff — deterministic routing improves reliability but reduces emergent behavior. For structured pipelines you typically prefer determinism.

[05:03] Maya: Let's walk through one of the specific failures you logged — the invoice parsing job. Jamal, you had a snippet?

[05:10] Jamal: Yeah, pasted in Slack earlier. On run 2025-09-05-101 the model produced this partial: '{"invoice_id": 12345, "amount": "USD 1,200", "items": [ {"desc": "Widget A" },' and then a blob of natural text. Our parser failed.

[05:27] Eliot: Classic case of natural language bleed. Two fixes: 1) stronger end-of-json marker like "<END_JSON>" after the object, which SDK strips, or 2) use the function-calling API that forces a JSON return type — it's generally more reliable. We can demo both.

[05:44] Priya: Which do you recommend for us? We have downstream systems consuming JSON, so fewer hacks preferred.

[05:49] Eliot: Use function-calling when you can; combine with schema enforcement. If you need streaming partials, use the <END_JSON> sentinel as a fallback.

[06:00] Maya: We'll include sample prompts and the SDK helper. I'll also attach a tiny Node demo that shows streaming partials + re-assembly.

[06:09] Jamal: Great. One more performance note — when we ran the local quantized model it was fast but output quality dipped. Any guidance on quantization profiles?

[06:19] Eliot: Yes, we have recommended quantization profiles tied to workload: 4-bit for high throughput with some quality loss, 8-bit for better fidelity. For completions with strict schema we suggest 8-bit or mixed precision while using prefix caching to reduce cost. I'll include a short doc with recommended knobs.

[06:36] Priya: Can you also provide regression test harness so we can run nightly checks? We want to guard against model drift.

[06:42] Maya: Redwood Optimize has a small eval harness we can share; for the POC we'll give you a lightweight runner that posts to your endpoint and compares outputs against golden prompts. Link: https://redwood.example.com/evals/poc-runner

[06:56] Hannah: On the compliance side, do you keep audit logs for function calls? Our auditors will ask for per-call metadata.

[07:03] Eliot: Yes, audit logs are available — timestamp, model version, function called, latency, and token usage. For Private deployments those logs sit in your retention; for hosted we retain per your plan.

[07:16] Jamal: Any gotchas with VPC peering for the private control plane? We tried to do that in a previous proof and networking was the blocker.

[07:24] Maya: We documented typical networking configs; in the last POC we had to open a couple of egress routes and set up a CIDR allowlist. We'll include a checklist for your infra team.

[07:36] Priya: Ok, to recap the deliverables?

[07:39] Maya: I'll read them out: 1) SDK snippet & small demo app showing tool/function calling + streaming partials and repaired JSON (Maya/Eliot) — due 2025-09-12. 2) Quantization and perf recommendations for your token distribution (Eliot) — due 2025-09-16. 3) Security and networking checklist and SOC2 docs (Maya) — 2025-09-12. 4) Bluehaven to run regression tests and share failing examples (Jamal) — due 2025-09-15. 5) Schedule dedicated-node benchmark (owners: Maya/Jamal) — week of 2025-09-22.

[08:10] Jamal: That sounds good. A small ask: can you include the exact SDK version and client flags you tested with? We had mismatches before where dev used 0.9.x and prod used 0.8.x and behaviors diverged.

[08:21] Eliot: Absolutely. We'll include the exact package.json/yarn.lock snippet and Dockerfile from our demo. Our current internal beta is redwood-sdk@0.10.3-beta.

[08:34] Priya: One last quick question — competitors. We evaluated Anthropic for a similar flow; their function-calling felt more deterministic in some cases. Any notes on that?

[08:42] Maya: We hear that. Anthropic tends to be conservative which can help determinism; Redwood focuses on configurability and observability. For POC we'll include a short note comparing expected behaviors and when you'd pick each approach.

[08:55] Hannah: Thanks, everyone. If no objections let's close and follow up in email.

[09:00] Maya: Thanks all. We'll shoot the artifacts after the call.

[09:05] (call ends)

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-hearings and filler. Artifacts referenced: https://redwood.example.com/sdk-examples/tool-calls, https://redwood.example.com/evals/poc-runner, /security/soc2.pdf.
